protocol.instrument_name: SA Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) Services – UTI Management Protocol
protocol.legal_basis: Authorisation page (p2): 'In accordance with the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services Scheme as determined by the Minister for Health and Wellbeing by notice in the Gazette on 2nd February 2024, registered pharmacists who have successfully completed training may supply specified antibiotic medicines without a prescription to eligible patients for the treatment of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).' Appendix 2 (p9): 'Sale or supply must comply with the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services Scheme as determined by the Minister for Health and Wellbeing by notice in the Gazette on 02/02/2024 and SA Community Pharmacy UTI Services – UTI Management Protocol.' Supply basis (p4): 'Supply, packaging and labelling of the approved medicines is in accordance with the Controlled Substances Act (1984) and the Controlled Substances (Poisons) Regulations 2011.'
protocol.supervision_model: Supply-without-prescription model under a Ministerial scheme (not prescribing under regulation 17A). Document's own terminology (p3 'Conditions'): the pharmacist 'has an unconditional general registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra)'; 'must comply with all relevant legislation, Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) and the Pharmacy Board of Australia's Code of Conduct'; 'Prior to providing services, the pharmacist must have successfully completed approved training as referred to in Appendix 1, and must maintain eligibility to provide services, including any ongoing training'; 'Community pharmacies registered by the Pharmacy Regulation Authority of South Australia (PRASA) may participate in the scheme'; the pharmacy must have 'a screened or private consulting area' with visual and auditory privacy. Assessment and eligibility decisions are made by the pharmacist ('after assessment by a pharmacist', 'as assessed by a pharmacist', p4).
protocol.scope_summary: SA Health UTI Management Protocol under the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services Scheme, providing 'a framework for pharmacists authorised to supply approved medicines for the management of suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) in eligible patients'. Service: 'timely access to advice, assessment and treatment for women with symptoms of uncomplicated UTI', complementary to other treatment services including GPs. Patient eligibility: women aged 18 to 65 years with an anatomical female urinary tract who are deemed likely to be experiencing an acute uncomplicated UTI after pharmacist assessment, at low risk of complications, and who meet inclusion criteria in relevant standards/guidelines/this protocol; ineligible: females aged under 18 and over 65 years, males, and individuals who have undergone gender reassignment surgery. Covers conditions (pharmacist, pharmacy, approved medicines), clinical documentation and communication, consultation fees, cultural safety, supplementary information (conservative management, antibiotic selection, urinalysis, patient information and referral, review), Appendix 1 training requirements, Appendix 2 approved medicines (trimethoprim first line, nitrofurantoin second line, cefalexin third line) and Appendix 3 references. Page 6 of the PDF contains no extractable text (the Clinical Flow Chart referenced by the companion fact sheet is presumed to be a page image).

inclusion.text: 'Eligible patients include women aged 18 to 65 years with an anatomical female urinary tract presenting to a community pharmacy:'
'o Who are deemed to be likely experiencing an acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection, after assessment by a pharmacist; and'
'o Who are at low risk of complications, as assessed by a pharmacist; and'
'o Who meet inclusion criteria in accordance with relevant professional practice standards, guidelines and this UTI Management Protocol.'

Service conditions that must hold before the eligibility assessment can be made: 'The pharmacist providing services has an unconditional general registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra).'; 'Prior to providing services, the pharmacist must have successfully completed approved training as referred to in Appendix 1, and must maintain eligibility to provide services, including any ongoing training.'; 'Community pharmacies registered by the Pharmacy Regulation Authority of South Australia (PRASA) may participate in the scheme.'; 'The pharmacy must have an area suitable to maintain confidentiality of the consultation, i.e. have a screened or private consulting area that: Ensures patients' privacy and confidentiality, including visual and auditory privacy; Has sufficient space to allow the presence of the patient, a carer if required, the pharmacist, and relevant documentation.'

exclusion.text: Appendix 1 training objective: 'The importance of referring a patient to a GP or other appropriate health service if risk factors for complicated UTI are present or a pharmacist is not confident that an uncomplicated UTI is a likely diagnosis.'

Supply constraint (not a patient characteristic, but blocks supply): 'The pharmacist must not sell or supply the medicines in a quantity that exceeds the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine.' and 'The pharmacist must only supply approved medicines as per requirements listed in Appendix 2.'

exclusion_exceptions.text: 'The services will increase options available for consumers to seek treatment and are complementary to other treatment services for UTI, including via general practitioners.' — a patient outside this service is not without treatment options; GP and other services remain available.

'Evidence based conservative management for uncomplicated UTI may include pain management and other non-prescription medicines. Non-pharmacological and self-care advice should also be provided.' — supply of an approved antibiotic is not the only permitted outcome of an eligible consultation.

'Pharmacists will ensure continuity of care and use their professional discretion to refer the patient to health professionals or services where appropriate, and where eligibility criteria are not met.' — failing eligibility leads to referral rather than to no care.

Age boundaries are inclusive as printed: 'women aged 18 to 65 years' (inclusion, p4) with ineligibility only for 'females aged under 18 years and over 65 years' (p4) — exactly 18 and exactly 65 remain eligible.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Assessment and antibiotic supply pathway for suspected uncomplicated UTI

steps.description: Conditions and clinical record: 'The pharmacist providing services has an unconditional general registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra).' 'The pharmacist must comply with all relevant legislation, Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) and the Pharmacy Board of Australia's Code of Conduct, and the expected standards of ethical behaviour of pharmacists towards individuals, the community and society.' 'Prior to providing services, the pharmacist must have successfully completed approved training as referred to in Appendix 1, and must maintain eligibility to provide services, including any ongoing training.' 'Community pharmacies registered by the Pharmacy Regulation Authority of South Australia (PRASA) may participate in the scheme.' 'The pharmacy must have an area suitable to maintain confidentiality of the consultation, i.e. have a screened or private consulting area that: Ensures patients' privacy and confidentiality, including visual and auditory privacy; Has sufficient space to allow the presence of the patient, a carer if required, the pharmacist, and relevant documentation.' Clinical documentation: 'The pharmacist must make a clinical record and a record in a pharmacy dispensing system regarding the supply of any antibiotics under these services.' The record must include: 'sufficient information to identify the patient; the name of the pharmacist who undertook the consultation and their healthcare identifier number (HPI-I); the date of the consultation; information relevant to the patient's diagnosis and treatment (for example, patient's medical history, adverse drug reactions); any clinical opinion reached, and actions taken by the pharmacist; details of any medication supplied for the patient (generic name, form, strength and quantity); any information or advice given by the pharmacist to the patient in relation to any proposed treatment; any consent given by a patient to the consultation, treatment proposed, sharing information with their medical practitioner.'

gates.criterion: pharmacist holds unconditional general registration with Ahpra
pharmacist has successfully completed approved training (Appendix 1) and maintains eligibility including any ongoing training
pharmacy is registered by PRASA
screened or private consulting area available with visual and auditory privacy and sufficient space

steps.description: Assessment and eligibility decision: 'Eligible patients include women aged 18 to 65 years with an anatomical female urinary tract presenting to a community pharmacy: o Who are deemed to be likely experiencing an acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection, after assessment by a pharmacist; and o Who are at low risk of complications, as assessed by a pharmacist; and o Who meet inclusion criteria in accordance with relevant professional practice standards, guidelines and this UTI Management Protocol.' 'Ineligible patients include females aged under 18 years and over 65 years, males, and individuals who have undergone gender reassignment surgery. UTIs in these groups are more likely be complicated and require referral to a general practitioner or other health service for further review.' Urinalysis/diagnostic probability (p7): 'The use of urinalysis by dipstick is not being mandated as part of the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services and is not a part of empiric treatment. The probability of cystitis is greater than 90% when at least two primary symptoms of cystitis are present, in the absence of vaginal discharge. Situations where there is a question over diagnosis of uncomplicated UTI should be referred to a medical practitioner for further assessment.' Antibiotic selection factors (p7): 'When selecting antibiotic treatment consider drug allergies, drug interactions and other contraindications.'

deemed likely experiencing an acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection, after assessment by a pharmacist (INC-2)

steps.description: Supply of approved medicines (Appendix 2, p9): 'Sale or supply must comply with the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services Scheme as determined by the Minister for Health and Wellbeing by notice in the Gazette on 02/02/2024 and SA Community Pharmacy UTI Services – UTI Management Protocol.' Approved oral antibiotics table — Trimethoprim (First line): '300mg orally, daily at night for 3 nights', maximum quantity '3 tablets or capsules', Conditions column blank; Nitrofurantoin (Second line): '100mg orally, every 6 hours for 5 days', maximum quantity '20 tablets or capsules', Conditions: 'Sale and supply limited to circumstances where trimethoprim is not appropriate for the patient or not available'; Cefalexin (Third line): '500mg orally, every 12 hours for 5 days', maximum quantity '10 tablets or capsules', Conditions: 'Sale and supply limited to circumstances where trimethoprim and nitrofurantoin are not appropriate for the patient or not available'. Supply rules (p3-p4): 'The pharmacist must only supply approved medicines as per requirements listed in Appendix 2.' 'The medicines are only sold or supplied to eligible patients in accordance with relevant professional practice standards and guidelines, and this UTI Management Protocol.' 'Supply, packaging and labelling of the approved medicines is in accordance with the Controlled Substances Act (1984) and the Controlled Substances (Poisons) Regulations 2011.' 'The pharmacist must not sell or supply the medicines in a quantity that exceeds the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine.' Antibiotic selection (p7): 'Recommendations for empiric antibiotic treatment are based on factors including efficacy, convenience, cost, availability, harms associated with antibiotic use (e.g. adverse effects in the patient, development of antibiotic resistance), resistance rates of common pathogens and a consideration of the risk of adverse outcomes from clinical failure.' 'When selecting antibiotic treatment consider drug allergies, drug interactions and other contraindications.' Conservative management (p7): 'Evidence based conservative management for uncomplicated UTI may include pain management and other non-prescription medicines. Non-pharmacological and self-care advice should also be provided.'

steps.description: Patient information, documentation and communication: 'Where a patient is prescribed medication, they should be given Consumer Medicines Information (CMI) about possible side effects (as per usual practice) and told to see their GP if symptoms worsen or are not resolved within 2 days.' 'Patients should be provided information about prevention of UTIs.' 'The pharmacist must offer a record of the treatment and consultation to the patient. This may include a copy of the checklist completed by the pharmacist during the consultation. The patient may choose to share this with their GP or other health professionals. Where possible, the patient should be actively encouraged to provide the consultation summary (patient checklist/outcome) to their GP, in order to have the episode of care recorded within their personal medical record at the general practice.' 'Following consent by the patient, the pharmacist may share a record of the supply and consultation with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one.' 'Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of the medicine supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient.' 'Pharmacists may charge a consultation fee for the service, in addition to the cost of any medicine that is supplied. Pharmacists should ensure that the patient understands the costs involved when offering the service.' 'Pharmacists must complete cultural safety and gender diversity training relevant to their place of practice, reflect on their competency and provide the service in ways that are inclusive, culturally safe, sensitive, and responsive.'

open_questions.topic: Page 6 of the PDF contains no extractable text — the Clinical Flow Chart is presumably a page image
open_questions.observed: Page 6 extracts as 'OFFICIAL' and page number '6' only. The companion fact sheet states the protocol 'includes a Clinical Flow Chart that provides information to guide assessment and clinical decision-making on management of uncomplicated UTI and appropriate referral'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Assessment criteria, symptom lists, red flags and referral branches held in the flow chart could not be transcribed and must not be invented; diagnosis_pathways was built only from the extractable prose (p3-p9).

open_questions.topic: Appendix 2 table columns — an extra strength value precedes each dosage with no separate column header in the extraction
open_questions.observed: Extracted rows read 'Trimethoprim 300mg 300mg orally, daily at night for 3 nights 3 tablets or capsules'; the header row reads 'Approved oral antibiotics Dosage Maximum quantity Conditions'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The leading value (300mg/100mg/500mg) has no visible header in the extraction; it is transcribed as 'strength' while the full dosage string is kept verbatim in 'dose'. Column assignment should be verified against the PDF page image.

open_questions.topic: No urgency tiers or referral destinations/timframes printed
open_questions.observed: Referral statements name only 'a general practitioner or other health service' / 'a medical practitioner' with no timeframes and no urgent or emergency tiers.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.urgent and referral.emergency are empty because the document genuinely prints none; destinations/timeframes must be supplied locally (see hugh_to_confirm).

open_questions.topic: Combinatorics of inclusion criteria are printed; exclusion grouping is derived
open_questions.observed: Inclusion sub-bullets are joined by 'and' (p4), supporting {all_of: [INC-1..INC-4]}; 'Ineligible patients include ...' introduces a list without an explicit any/all label.
open_questions.why_unclear: Exclusion groups default to any_of (any single listed ineligibility excludes), recorded here per spec rule 4.

open_questions.topic: 'Anatomical female urinary tract' and 'individuals who have undergone gender reassignment surgery' are not defined
open_questions.observed: Both phrases are printed in the eligibility section (p4) with no definitions, while p5 requires pharmacists to 'complete cultural safety and gender diversity training relevant to their place of practice, reflect on their competency and provide the service in ways that are inclusive, culturally safe, sensitive, and responsive.'
open_questions.why_unclear: The operational meaning of these eligibility terms (and how they interact with the cultural safety requirement) is not stated; transcribed verbatim with confidence 'high' for the text but the interpretation is flagged for local confirmation.

open_questions.topic: 'Risk factors for complicated UTI' are never enumerated in this protocol
open_questions.observed: p4 refers to patients 'at low risk of complications, as assessed by a pharmacist'; p8 requires 'referring a patient to a GP ... if risk factors for complicated UTI are present'. The actual list is not printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: It is delegated to the approved training programs and clinical guidelines; no criteria could be transcribed without inventing them.

open_questions.topic: 'Primary symptoms of cystitis' are not enumerated
open_questions.observed: 'The probability of cystitis is greater than 90% when at least two primary symptoms of cystitis are present, in the absence of vaginal discharge.' (p7)
open_questions.why_unclear: The individual symptoms are not listed anywhere in the extractable text (they may be in the page-6 flow chart); RF-9 is therefore derived from the printed probability statement with confidence 'medium'.

open_questions.topic: Role of dipstick urinalysis left open
open_questions.observed: 'The use of urinalysis by dipstick is not being mandated as part of the Community Pharmacy Urinary Tract Infection Services and is not a part of empiric treatment.' (p7)
open_questions.why_unclear: The document says it is not mandated and not part of empiric treatment but does not say whether it may be used; no rule derived.

open_questions.topic: 'Smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack' — pack sizes not printed
open_questions.observed: 'The pharmacist must not sell or supply the medicines in a quantity that exceeds the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine.' (p4) alongside Appendix 2 maximum quantities (3, 20 and 10 tablets or capsules).
open_questions.why_unclear: Actual pack sizes per product/brand are not printed, so the operative supply quantity for each product cannot be determined from this document alone.

open_questions.topic: Appendix 2 maximum quantity vs pack ceiling interaction
open_questions.observed: Appendix 2 prints maximum quantities (trimethoprim 3 tablets or capsules; nitrofurantoin 20; cefalexin 10) while p4 prints the smallest-manufacturer-pack ceiling.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state which ceiling governs if they differ; both recorded in the treatment rows.

open_questions.topic: Trimethoprim row has a blank Conditions cell
open_questions.observed: In the extracted Appendix 2 table the Conditions text appears only for nitrofurantoin and cefalexin.
open_questions.why_unclear: Assumed to mean no additional supply condition applies to first-line trimethoprim; confirm visually against the PDF in case text was lost in extraction.

open_questions.topic: Relationship to the SA Health Urinary Tract Infections (adult): Empirical Treatment Clinical Guideline
open_questions.observed: 'The SA Health Urinary Tract Infections (adult): Empirical Treatment Clinical Guideline is also in place in South Australia. This protocol is based upon these evidence-based guidelines.' (p3) — but no local-modification rule is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Whether that guideline can alter first-line selection for this scheme is not stated; Appendix 2 is the operative list.

open_questions.topic: Consultation fee amount and disclosure mechanics
open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists may charge a consultation fee for the service, in addition to the cost of any medicine that is supplied. Pharmacists should ensure that the patient understands the costs involved when offering the service.' (p5)
open_questions.why_unclear: No amount, cap or disclosure format is printed.

open_questions.topic: Mapping of printed wording to red-flag actions/severity
open_questions.observed: 'Ineligible patients include ...' → NOT_ELIGIBLE/medium; 'should be referred ... for further assessment' → REVIEW_GP/medium; 'should be referred to a general practitioner or other health service' → REFER/medium; pack and line-of-therapy supply rules → NOT_ELIGIBLE/medium.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document prints no urgency language at all; severity set to 'medium' uniformly rather than upgraded, per spec rule 3.

open_questions.topic: Gate on_fail values not stated by the document for most steps
open_questions.observed: Branch outcomes are implied by 'require referral' / 'should be referred' wording but are not printed as flow logic (and the flow chart that would show them is on the non-extractable page 6).
open_questions.why_unclear: Used SEE_PW-1-S6 to route failed eligibility/diagnosis gates into the referral step, STOP for service-condition and supply-rule failures, and 'unclear' where the document states no consequence (spec rule 5).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Full content of the Clinical Flow Chart on page 6 (image) — assessment criteria, symptom checklist, red flags and referral branches.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The fact sheet says the protocol includes a Clinical Flow Chart guiding assessment, decision-making and referral; none of it is in extractable text. The engine's diagnosis pathway is incomplete without it.

hugh_to_confirm.item: The enumerated list of 'risk factors for complicated UTI' and the list of 'primary symptoms of cystitis'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Both are referenced but never printed; gates INC-2/INC-3 and RF-9 cannot be evaluated as hard checks until the lists are supplied from the training/guideline sources.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Product-level pack sizes for trimethoprim 300mg, nitrofurantoin 100mg and cefalexin 500mg — what is 'the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The supply ceiling is defined by pack size, which is not printed; interacts with the Appendix 2 maximum quantities (3/20/10).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Local interpretation of 'anatomical female urinary tract' and 'individuals who have undergone gender reassignment surgery' against the cultural safety and gender diversity training requirement.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Printed eligibility terms are undefined and potentially in tension with the p5 cultural safety obligation; local policy must define how eligibility is assessed and explained.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Referral destinations, contact pathways and timeframes for each referral rule (GP, other health service, medical practitioner), including after-hours and escalation arrangements.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: No destinations, timeframes or urgency tiers are printed anywhere in the protocol.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Whether dipstick urinalysis may be used in the consultation ('not being mandated ... is not a part of empiric treatment').
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Permission is neither granted nor denied; affects what the pharmacist may record and rely on.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verification process for pharmacist eligibility: approved training completion (Appendix 1), ongoing training currency, Ahpra unconditional general registration and HPI-I recording.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Conditions are stated but the evidence/recording process for each supply event is not printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: My Health Record upload mechanics — consent wording, what is uploaded, handling of 'unless requested otherwise by the patient', and the dispensing-system record fields.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The obligation is printed but the operational detail (fields, timing, opt-out record) is left to local process.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Consultation fee setting, amount and the required cost-disclosure format.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Pharmacists may charge a consultation fee' with no amount or disclosure standard printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Reconciliation of Appendix 2 first-line trimethoprim with the SA Health Urinary Tract Infections (adult): Empirical Treatment Clinical Guideline.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The protocol says it is 'based upon' that guideline but prints no rule for when the guideline and Appendix 2 differ.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Format, content and periodicity of the data provided 'at the request of the Minister for Health and Wellbeing'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Mandatory but unspecified; a data-specification decision for the service.

hugh_to_confirm.item: PRASA pharmacy registration verification and the standard for 'a screened or private consulting area' (visual and auditory privacy, sufficient space).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Service condition printed without an assessment standard or evidence requirement.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Operational meaning of the nitrofurantoin/cefalexin Conditions — what counts as 'not appropriate for the patient' (allergy, interaction, availability, local resistance).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Second/third-line supply is conditional on this judgement but the criteria are not printed; supply outside the conditions is a compliance breach.
